- [2023/05/26] Repudiation occurs when a party shows an unwillingness or inability to perform substantial obligations under a contract.
- [2023/05/26] Repudiation is considered a breach of contract and can lead to termination and damages.
- [2023/05/26] The user emphasized the importance of engaging lawyers early and avoiding certain statements that could be considered repudiation.
- [2023/05/26] Repudiation is not the same as termination but can lead to it if the repudiatory conduct is not remedied.
- [2023/05/26] Accepting repudiation allows the innocent party to terminate the contract and claim damages.
- [2023/05/26] It is not proper to sue specifically for repudiation; rather, one would bring a claim for breach of contract.
- [2023/05/26] Proving a repudiatory breach requires considering the context and providing the at-fault party opportunities to rectify the breach.
- [2023/05/26] Responding to accusations of repudiation is crucial to avoid being seen as engaging in repudiatory conduct.
- [2023/05/26] Courts assess repudiation based on breaches of essential or non-essential terms and the specific facts of the case.
- [2023/05/26] Best practices include documenting all communication, seeking legal advice, and responding promptly to suspected repudiation.
